title: Why both games wait for the input pair
caption: Conceptual lockstep sequence, not a packet capture or latency measurement. k labels a gameplay tick. Checkpoints occur later at agreed ticks; the retained prototype checks every 120 ticks. Missing input waits; differing checkpoint hashes stop the session. There is no rollback.

steps.label: Inputs
steps.title: Each player submits an input
steps.detail: Both devices produce their own controller state for the same scheduled tick.

steps.label: Pair
steps.title: Both copies receive the same pair
steps.detail: The relay shares P1 and P2 input together. It does not compute or stream the game.

steps.label: Advance
steps.title: Each game can advance one tick
steps.detail: Both copies use the agreed pair. Input availability allows progress; identical game state also depends on deterministic execution.

steps.label: Check
steps.title: Compare state at a later checkpoint
steps.detail: Matching hashes at the same checkpoint allow the session to continue. These illustrative equality signs are not captured game hashes.

steps.label: Inputs
steps.title: Only P1's input has arrived
steps.detail: P1's input is ready, but the input pair is incomplete. A faster device cannot guess the other player's action.

steps.label: Wait
steps.title: Hold the tick while input is missing
steps.detail: The prototype waits instead of predicting an input. Waiting changes wall-clock progress, not the agreed input pair.

steps.label: Arrive
steps.title: The delayed input completes the pair
steps.detail: Once P2 arrives, both devices can receive the complete pair for that tick.

steps.label: Advance
steps.title: Resume from the same tick
steps.detail: Each device advances using the agreed input. This is lockstep waiting, not rollback or a measured network delay.

steps.label: Inputs
steps.title: Both inputs can arrive normally
steps.detail: Matching controls alone do not guarantee matching state. Disc-completion timing was one cause of divergence in the earlier prototype.

steps.label: Pair
steps.title: Share the agreed input pair
steps.detail: The transport supplies the same pair to both games. It does not inspect every simulation instruction.

steps.label: Advance
steps.title: A hidden difference can still accumulate
steps.detail: Each copy advances locally. The later checkpoint tests whether their state stayed aligned.

steps.label: Stop
steps.title: A differing checkpoint stops the session
steps.detail: The current prototype stops on disagreement. It does not rewind, repair the state or resume automatically.
